unit.title: What agents are, and when to trust them

lesson.title: A person stays in charge
lesson.subtitle: Reading is fine; acting needs your yes

video.title: A person stays in charge
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Dr Farah Rahman — university lecturer in education, Bangladesh (main character)
Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: Never hand these over, and the lab

scenes.visual: A list: The wrong week; It asked first.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: An agent nearly sent a message to all our parents: the trip to the farm is cancelled! It wasn’t. Someone had typed the wrong week. Thank goodness it asked me first.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: why a person stays in charge of what an agent does.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some tools only read: the weather, the timetable, the library. Others act: they send a message, set a reminder, or change a record. A wrong action can reach a parent, or change a child’s record.

scenes.visual: A list: It shows exactly what it will do; It waits; You read every word; You say yes or no.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So an agent should ask before it acts. It shows you exactly what it will do, and waits. You read it, and say yes or no. That’s called approval.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Darsi Tiny learned this. Ask it to send Mrs Mensah a message, and it replies with the exact words: shall I send this? Please reply yes or no. Say no, and nothing is sent.

scenes.visual: A list: Learned behaviour can fail; “Yes, send it” alone: it invents one; The app blocks it in code; And you decide.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: But asking first is learned, and learned behaviour can fail. Type only, yes, send it, and it makes up a message. So the app checks in code too, and blocks it: no one was asked. The real guards are the code, and you.

scenes.visual: A list: Read only: look things up; Ask first: after your yes; Allowed: small, safe jobs.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: You can choose what an agent may do. Read only: it can look things up, but not act. Ask first: it acts only after your yes. Allowed: it acts on its own, for small, safe jobs.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! The agent asks: shall I tell all parents that sports day moves to Friday? You’re not sure it’s Friday. What do you do?

scenes.visual: A list: Not sure? Say no; Read every word; Sent can’t be unsent.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Say no, and check the date first. Approval only protects you if you read what you approve. And once a message is sent, you can’t take it back.

scenes.visual: A list: Passwords and accounts; Pupils’ private details; Decisions about a child.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some things never go to an agent at all. Your passwords and your accounts. Pupils’ private details, like health, family or marks, unless a school rule allows it. And decisions about a child stay with people.

scenes.visual: A list: Ask first: no, then yes; Read only: a reminder?; Code check off, then on.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, choose Ask first and send the message to Mrs Mensah: deny it, then approve it. Choose Read only, and ask for a reminder. Then switch the code check off, and see why it matters.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. An agent wants to send a message to all parents. Who should approve it?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Acting needs your yes; The app checks in code too; Some things stay with people.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Acting needs your yes · The app checks in code too · Some things stay with people
scenes.narration: A teacher who has read every word. Remember: reading is fine, but acting needs your yes. A model’s asking can fail, so the app checks too. And passwords, private data and decisions about children stay with people.

scenes.visual: A list: Play “Yes or no?”; The agent shows a message; Read it, then vote; One hides a mistake.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play Yes or no? A pupil plays the agent and shows a message card: shall I send this? The class reads it and votes. Hide a mistake in one card.

checkpoints.prompt: The agent asks: “Shall I tell all parents that sports day moves to Friday?” You’re not sure it’s Friday. What do you do?

options.text: Say no, and check the date first
Say yes, and fix it later

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — approval only protects you if you read and check what you approve. A sent message can’t be taken back.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a polite question isn’t a reason to say yes, and a sent message can’t be unsent. Say no and check first.

checkpoints.prompt: An agent wants to send a message to all parents. Who should approve it?

options.text: A teacher who has read the exact message

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a person who has read every word approves, and the app checks in code that someone really did.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — an agent can’t approve its own actions, and a message to every family matters. A person who read it approves.
